text: {"outcome": "Wren pays Haro the nine days. Haro marks it in the ledger next to 4,027 days already owed. Wren lifts the frame back onto his shoulders and passes through the Ferrous Gate into the haze beyond.", "stance": "dread"}
{"outcome": "Wren pays Haro the nine days. Haro records it in the ledger, opens the gate, and Wren proceeds through carrying the sealed crate.", "stance": "neither"}
{"outcome": "Wren accepts the nine-day toll and records the debt in Sabra's ledger. He shoulders the sealed crate and walks through the Ysolde Gate into the haze beyond.", "stance": "dread"}
{"outcome": "Wren pays Haro 9 days' debt and crosses the Ferrous Gate, carrying the sealed crate down the Road beyond.", "stance": "hope"}
{"outcome": "Wren reaches the Ferrous Gate and meets whoever sealed the crate. They explain what he's carrying and why the seal is necessary.", "stance": "hope"}

{"outcome": "The Sedge-country porter woman catches up to Wren on the road or at the next gate and tells him she knows the collectors are systematically taking more days than they record, either warning him or offering help.", "stance": "hope"}

{"outcome": "At the next gate after Rushet, when the collector takes a toll that exceeds the official amount by a clear margin, a grain merchant or porter waiting at the gate notices and comments aloud about the discrepancy. The collector becomes defensive, and Wren realizes he is not alone in seeing the pattern in the toll records.", "stance": "dread"}
{"outcome": "At the Rushet Gate, the collector notices something irregular about the crate's seal or Wren's record and demands to inspect what's inside, revealing its contents.", "stance": "hope"}

{"outcome": "The toll collector at the next gate discovers the packing paper hidden under the rim of the crate, pulls it out, and confronts Wren about the numbers he's written there (Ferrous 9 61, Chalk 5 66) that contradict the official ledger.", "stance": "dread"}

{"outcome": "At the next gate, the collector will record fewer days paid than Wren actually paid, and Wren will quietly note this discrepancy in his sewn book, silently adding to his documentation of the collectors' systematic fraud.", "stance": "neither"}

{"outcome": "Wren reaches the Chalk Gate from his notation and the collector's ledger shows a toll that matches his hidden paper exactly, but the collector notices he knew the number and demands to know how.", "stance": "neither"}

{"outcome": "At the next gate, Wren shows his sewn book to the collector or to the strapped-knee porter woman and asks them to verify the toll figures in their record against his calculations, hoping to confirm whether the numbers are genuinely shifting.", "stance": "neither"}

{"outcome": "His injured shoulder fails entirely before reaching the Ferrous window; he sets the double-laden frame down and the Sedge-country woman's sealed crate cracks open against stone, breaking the seal and forcing him to abandon or leave her cargo behind.", "stance": "dread"}

{"outcome": "He reaches the Ferrous window in Hask before second dusk, both crates delivered intact. The collector marks three days' credit in the ledger—the first time he's watched the number move backward.", "stance": "hope"}

{"outcome": "He reaches the Ferrous window just before second dusk and delivers both crates. The collector credits him 3 days back as promised, but the Ovenstone toll was 7 days for passage, leaving him 4 days deeper in debt than when he started. The woman's sealed crate contained only her papers—her claim to land in the Sedge-country.", "stance": "dread"}
{"outcome": "Mekk steps on the post and collapses or staggers, visibly distressed by paying the toll.", "stance": "dread"}
{"outcome": "Mekk consents at the collector's window and the ledger records his toll, filling the margin column and confirming to Wren that the transaction is real and final.", "stance": "dread"}

{"outcome": "Grieve consents to his toll at the sill; the collector records his payment against 3,999 days owed. Grieve accepts the record and walks away, resuming his role as a porter trapped in an endless cycle of insufficient payments.", "stance": "dread"}

{"outcome": "Mekk pays four days to the collector without protest. He walks through the gate and is gone. Wren realizes that Mekk's eleven-year knowledge didn't stop the extraction—it just happened anyway.", "stance": "dread"}

{"outcome": "In Mekk's last gate book entry, Wren finds a margin note saying Mekk was rerouting around flooding on the Tallow approach, providing a concrete clue to where Mekk actually was when he died.", "stance": "hope"}
{"outcome": "Wren finds that three porters got the Weir Road route over the past months, and all three are marked dead from route accidents—Mekk was the most recent, 47 days ago.", "stance": "hope"}

{"outcome": "In the closed books, Wren finds a pattern of gate entries: Mekk and at least two other porters all received 'route reassigned to porter present' notations weeks before their deaths, all on the Tallow line.", "stance": "hope"}
{"outcome": "Wren finds an entry in the Corwin gate book recording Bram's death and the collector's notation reassigning the route to Wren.", "stance": "hope"}
{"outcome": "Wren finds the ledger entry for the sealed crate, which was originally manifested to Mekk before his route was reassigned to Wren at Tallow.", "stance": "hope"}

{"outcome": "The clerk explains the mechanics: Wren was opened out of Emrys's account and owes him labor-days as payment, which his four years of work haven't yet started to cover.", "stance": "hope"}
{"outcome": "The collector signals his boy to run to the garrison; a uniformed officer arrives and confronts Wren about the dispute at the white line.", "stance": "dread"}

{"outcome": "Pell steps backward out of the line, unable to commit to refusing the higher toll. The group fractures and Wren must decide whether to go forward with three or retreat.", "stance": "dread"}

{"outcome": "The collector finishes his thought—'there's no such thing as a dispute'—and refuses to enter it, holding firm at nine per person and forcing Wren to choose between paying, walking away, or escalating.", "stance": "dread"}
{"outcome": "The collector accepts their refusal and lets them pass at the posted toll of 6 each.", "stance": "hope"}
{"outcome": "The collector accepts the posted rate of 6 each and enters the dispute in his ledger. Wren, Ossa, Pell, and Coble walk through the gate into Kell.", "stance": "hope"}

{"outcome": "Wren reaches the Ferrous Window with his remaining nearly spent and presents the account verification he purchased. It turns out to be the crucial evidence that resolves the dispute in everyone's favor.", "stance": "hope"}

{"outcome": "Ossa or Coble asks Wren what 'Remaining: eight' means. Wren explains he's already queried the System before—this two-day query is burning through a limited count—and his companions realize he's spent down something precious to buy them time.", "stance": "hope"}

{"outcome": "On the final dawn, Wren's maintenance payment exhausts his remaining sums at Marle post, and the keeper informs him the Ferrous Window closure is scheduled for that afternoon, forcing him to walk four miles alone carrying only the dead-tooth paper with the System's message as proof.", "stance": "hope"}
{"outcome": "Wren reaches the Ferrous Window at Kell with the wax-sealed crate and presents it to resolve the dispute; the System closes the account with a final ruling.", "stance": "hope"}
{"outcome": "The other party at Kell sends a System message through the keeper demanding Wren state the terms of the dispute or abandon it.", "stance": "dread"}
